misconception: Real developers do everything by hand — an agent in your codebase is a gimmick.

mentorLessons.line: Claude Code isn't a chat window — it's an agent at your anvil. It reads your codebase, edits files, and runs commands itself, working across many files to get things done.
Learn the rhythm of the forge: it finds the right files, shows you the proposed change, asks your approval, then strikes. You remain the master — it swings the hammer.
A CLAUDE.md at the project root is read at the start of every session. Write down what you'd otherwise re-explain — build commands, conventions, rules — and keep it specific and concise.
Permission modes set how often the agent pauses for your word. In plan mode it only reads and proposes — nothing touches your files until you approve the plan.
A slash commands the session itself: /clear for an empty context, /compact to summarize and free space, /permissions to set the rules, /resume to pick up an old thread.
When a side-quest would flood your main conversation with search results, send a subagent. It works in its own context window and returns only the summary.
Instructions shape behavior; hooks guarantee it. A hook is a shell command that always runs at a lifecycle point — format after every edit, or block a forbidden file before it's touched.
MCP connects the forge to the outside world — issue trackers, databases, design tools — so Claude acts on them directly instead of working from what you paste. But verify you trust each server first.
Speak git in plain words — 'commit my changes,' 'create a PR.' And when two tasks must run at once, give each session its own worktree so the edits never collide.

questions.prompt: A veteran on your team scoffs: "An AI in the codebase is just autocomplete with extra steps." What actually sets Claude Code apart from a chat assistant?
choices: It only suggests snippets that you paste in yourself
It's mainly a faster search engine for documentation
It's agentic — it reads your codebase, edits files, and runs commands itself
It replaces version control entirely
questions.reteach: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool: it reads your codebase, edits files, and runs commands itself — not just a text suggester.
hardChoices: It's a chat assistant with a bigger context window for pasted code
It autocompletes lines in your editor as you type, like an IDE plugin
It runs your code in a cloud sandbox so nothing executes on your machine

questions.prompt: You launch Claude Code inside a huge unfamiliar repo and ask "what does this project do?" Do you have to paste files in first?
choices: No — it reads your project files as needed; you don't manually add context
Yes — it can only see text you paste into the chat
Yes — but only files shorter than a screen
No — but only if the repo has no subfolders
questions.reteach: Claude Code reads your project files as needed — you don't have to manually feed it context.
hardChoices: No — but only files referenced in CLAUDE.md are loaded automatically
Yes — you must add each folder with /add-dir before files are readable
No — but each file read needs manual approval unless you exit plan mode

questions.prompt: You ask Claude Code to "add input validation to the signup form." What's the standard flow before anything changes on disk?
choices: It edits silently and mentions it afterward
It finds the file, shows the proposed changes, asks for approval, then makes the edit
It mails you a patch to apply by hand
It refuses until you write the code yourself
questions.reteach: The loop is: find the right file, show proposed changes, ask your approval, then edit — you stay in control.
hardChoices: It switches into plan mode automatically for any request that edits files
It edits right away — approval prompts only apply to bash commands
A PreToolUse hook must approve the edit before Claude is allowed to act

questions.prompt: You're about to attempt a major change in a system you barely understand. Per the docs, the strongest opening move is to...
choices: Type the change request fast before the context fills up
Turn off all permission prompts so nothing interrupts
Ask for the entire app to be rewritten in one prompt
Let Claude explore first — start with broad questions about the code, then narrow down
questions.reteach: Let Claude analyze and understand the code first — broad questions, then narrow — before asking for changes.
hardChoices: Write the full plan into CLAUDE.md yourself before opening the session
Hand the whole change to a subagent so your main context stays clean
Switch to acceptEdits so exploration isn't slowed by approval prompts

questions.prompt: Every session you re-explain the same three things: the build command, the test command, and "never touch the legacy folder." What's the documented fix?
choices: Put them in a CLAUDE.md at the project root — it's read at the start of every session
Keep re-typing them; there's no persistence mechanism
Hide the legacy folder so it can't be found
Bury them in a code comment and hope
questions.reteach: CLAUDE.md holds persistent instructions Claude reads at the start of every session — write down what you'd otherwise re-explain.
hardChoices: Add them to README.md — Claude reads it at the start of every session
Save them as a custom slash command and run it at each session start
Add them as permission rules in settings so they're always enforced

questions.prompt: Which of these belongs in a well-written CLAUDE.md, going by the docs' guidance on specificity?
choices: "Format code properly"
"Be careful with important files"
"Run npm test before committing"
"Write good code"
questions.reteach: Write instructions concrete enough to verify — 'Run npm test before committing' beats vague advice like 'test your changes.'
hardChoices: "Use clean code principles throughout the project"
"A full architecture overview copied in from the README"
"A changelog of every past Claude Code session"

questions.prompt: You want Claude to research a risky refactor and lay out its whole approach — but not touch a single source file until you've read the proposal. Which mode?
choices: acceptEdits — it reviews changes after the fact
Plan mode — Claude reads and explores but doesn't edit until you approve the plan
bypassPermissions — fastest is safest
No such mode exists; you must watch every keystroke
questions.reteach: Plan mode tells Claude to research and propose changes without making them — edits stay blocked until you approve the plan.
hardChoices: acceptEdits — edits are proposed but held until you end the session
A deny rule on the Edit tool — that's what plan mode is under the hood
Delegate it to the Explore subagent — research always happens there

questions.prompt: A settings rule denies "git push", but your prompt tells Claude "you're totally allowed to push." What happens when it tries?
choices: The prompt wins — instructions override settings
The conflict makes the session halt with an error
Claude gains push access for one command only
The deny rule wins — permission rules are enforced by Claude Code itself, not by what the model is told
questions.reteach: Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not the model — prompts and CLAUDE.md shape what Claude tries, not what's allowed.
hardChoices: CLAUDE.md instructions can override settings rules, but prompts cannot
Claude Code asks you to confirm, since the prompt and settings disagree
The deny rule only applies in plan mode, so the push goes through

questions.prompt: You finished one task and are starting a completely unrelated one, but the context is stuffed with the old work. Cheapest reset?
choices: /clear — start a new conversation with empty context
/compact — it deletes the conversation entirely
/resume — it wipes the current session
/model — a new model means a fresh context
questions.reteach: /clear starts a fresh conversation with empty context; /compact instead summarizes so you can continue the same task with more room.
hardChoices: /compact — it summarizes the old task so the new one starts clean
/resume — starting a resumed thread flushes the current context
Quit and relaunch the CLI — context can't be emptied mid-session

questions.prompt: Your team repeats the same multi-step code-review workflow constantly. How do you turn it into a one-liner like /review-pr?
choices: You can't — only built-in commands exist
File a feature request and wait for Anthropic to build it
Create a custom skill — a markdown file your team can share, invoked with a slash
Write a separate wrapper program around the CLI
questions.reteach: Custom slash commands are skills — shareable markdown files that package a repeatable workflow, like /review-pr.
hardChoices: Register a hook that fires whenever you type /review-pr
Add the steps to CLAUDE.md — headings there become slash commands
Create a subagent named review-pr — subagents are invoked with a slash

questions.prompt: Answering one question means sweeping hundreds of files, and you don't want search dumps drowning your main conversation. The docs-recommended move?
choices: Paste every file in manually and scroll
Delegate to a subagent — it explores in its own context window and returns only the summary
Ask the same question repeatedly until it sticks
Disable file reading to keep the context small
questions.reteach: A subagent does the heavy exploration in its own context and reports back just the findings, keeping your main conversation clean.
hardChoices: Run /compact between searches so the dumps keep getting summarized
Use plan mode — file reads there don't consume the main context
Add a PostToolUse hook that strips search output from the context

questions.prompt: Which of these is true of the built-in Explore subagent?
choices: It edits files as it searches to save time
It requires a separate subscription to enable
It replaces the main conversation once launched
It's read-only — built for searching and analyzing code, with write and edit denied
questions.reteach: Explore is a fast read-only subagent for searching and analyzing codebases — its write and edit tools are denied.
hardChoices: It can edit, but each edit is escalated to the main session for approval
It's read-only because it always runs in plan mode by default
It's a slash command — run /explore to sweep the codebase

questions.prompt: You want your formatter to run after every single file edit — guaranteed, not "hopefully remembered." Which mechanism?
choices: A PostToolUse hook — hooks run deterministically at lifecycle events
A polite request in CLAUDE.md
Reminding Claude at the start of each session
A subagent that watches for edits
questions.reteach: Hooks are shell commands that always execute at lifecycle points — a PostToolUse hook guarantees formatting after edits, no reliance on the model choosing to.
hardChoices: A PreToolUse hook — it fires right after the edit completes
A CLAUDE.md rule — memory files are re-read after every edit
A formatter subagent that watches the main agent's edits

questions.prompt: How can a PreToolUse hook protect a sensitive file like .env from being modified?
choices: It can't — hooks can only log what happened
It hides the file from directory listings only
The hook script can block the edit before it runs, and Claude receives feedback explaining why
It encrypts the file when Claude approaches
questions.reteach: A PreToolUse hook runs before the action and can block it — Claude gets an explanation of why, so it adjusts its approach.
hardChoices: It can only block edits if plan mode is also active in the session
It can warn Claude, but only a permission rule can actually block a tool
It blocks the edit silently — Claude never learns why the write failed

questions.prompt: You keep copy-pasting Jira tickets and database rows into your Claude Code session. What's the documented better way?
choices: Keep pasting — that's the intended workflow
Connect those tools via MCP so Claude can read and act on them directly
Retype the tickets into a text file first
Only work from screenshots of the other tools
questions.reteach: MCP servers connect Claude Code to external tools like issue trackers and databases, so it acts on them directly instead of on what you paste.
hardChoices: List the Jira URLs in CLAUDE.md so Claude refetches them every session
Add a hook that injects the ticket text into each prompt automatically
Spawn a subagent — only subagents can reach tools outside the repo

questions.prompt: Before connecting a third-party MCP server, the docs specifically warn you to...
choices: Verify you trust it first — servers that fetch external content can expose you to prompt injection risk
Do nothing special — every MCP server is vetted by Anthropic
Grant it full permissions immediately so it works
Delete your CLAUDE.md so instructions can't conflict
questions.reteach: Verify you trust each MCP server before connecting — servers that fetch external content can carry prompt injection risk.
hardChoices: Enable plan mode first — MCP tools can't run until a plan is approved
Confirm it's in an official registry — listed servers are pre-vetted
Deny its tools in CLAUDE.md until you have tested each one yourself

questions.prompt: Feature work in one terminal, a bug fix in another — same repo, two Claude sessions. How do you keep their edits from colliding?
choices: You can't run two sessions on one repo
Have both edit the main branch and merge by luck
Run each session in its own git worktree — separate checkouts on their own branches
Turn git off until both finish
questions.reteach: Worktrees give each parallel session a separate checkout on its own branch, so concurrent edits don't collide.
hardChoices: Run the bug fix in plan mode — read-only sessions can't collide
Give each session its own branch in the same checkout — git keeps them apart
Use a subagent for the bug fix — subagents get an isolated checkout

questions.prompt: You closed your laptop mid-task yesterday. How do you pick the work back up today without re-explaining everything?
choices: You can't — sessions vanish when closed
Resume the conversation — Claude Code saves every conversation locally, so you continue where you left off
Recite yesterday's chat from memory as a new prompt
Delete the repo and start clean
questions.reteach: Conversations are saved locally — resume the most recent one (or pick from a list) instead of re-explaining context.
hardChoices: Ask Claude to reread CLAUDE.md — session history is appended there
Run /compact — it restores a summary of the previous session
Sign in and sync — history is stored on Anthropic's servers, not locally
